clue.text: Colourless, inferior player responsible for the hole Alice got into

definitions.text: responsible for the hole Alice got into

parts.note: white is the absence of colour, so colourless gives WHITE
a rabbit is slang for a poor player, as at cricket, golf or tennis

explanation.surface: A pale, weak player is blamed for the hole a girl named Alice fell into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is British sporting slang for a hopeless player, especially a poor batsman in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's story the hurrying creature in a waistcoat leads Alice down the burrow into Wonderland.

clue.text: Drag through the lobby, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for lobby is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a hall is an entrance lobby

explanation.surface: Someone is pulling a heavy load through a building's entrance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul is to pull something heavy along: a synonym of drag.

clue.text: Turn to a different course of hard ship's biscuit?

explanation.surface: A ship changes course, perhaps because of its rock-hard biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing boat changes course by going about into the wind; hardtack (often just tack) was the dry biscuit sailors ate at sea.

clue.text: Esteem directed to sceptre

indicators.note: directed here means steered or arranged anew, so the letters of sceptre are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monarch's regard is pointed towards the royal staff of office.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem and respect are synonyms for the high regard one has for someone.

clue.text: Principal target for the bellows-maker

explanation.surface: The main aim for whoever makes bellows for the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bellows' looks like the fireside air pump, but it is the plural verb: the creature that bellows.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of a dartboard or target is called the bull; a bull is also an animal that bellows, or roars.

clue.text: Perfectly conceived excuse, initially, I play around

indicators.note: around says that I and the word for play go round the letter taken from excuse

parts.note: to dally is to play or trifle idly

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter only of the word excuse

explanation.surface: Someone offers a well-thought-out excuse for fooling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes E from 'excuse'; 'around' puts I and DALLY round it, the E landing after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in an ideal way is done perfectly, as best it could be imagined.

clue.text: Seriously tackle the locks with something stronger than hairpins?

definitions.text: the locks with something stronger than hairpins?

explanation.surface: Someone sets about doing their hair with sturdier clips than pins.
explanation.walkthrough: Hair grips are clips that hold locks of hair; locks given grips have been brought to them.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to grips with a problem is to deal with it in earnest; hair held by clips has had grips applied.

clue.text: Appropriate cash for occasional use

parts.note: read one way it is to steal funds by slipping them into your trouser pouch; read another it is a small allowance for minor spending

explanation.surface: Someone suitably sets aside a little money for occasional spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective meaning suitable, but it is the verb: to take for oneself, as you would by slipping it into your clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A small regular allowance, often given to children, for incidental spending.

clue.text: Commotion as young Dorothy spins round and round

indicators.note: spins round says that the short name for Dorothy is turned back to front

parts.note: Dot is a pet form of the name Dorothy, as used for a little girl
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A small girl twirling and twirling causes a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young Dorothy' is a pet name, and 'spins round' turns it back to front; the second 'round' is a separate letter, not more spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a fuss or kerfuffle, a synonym of commotion.

clue.text: Lively Long John records a rise in temperature

definitions.note: the definition is a description of what the substance does, so it is a verb phrase standing for a noun

parts.note: quick in its old sense means alive or lively
Long John Silver is the pirate in Stevenson's Treasure Island

explanation.surface: An energetic pirate keeps notes when the weather warms up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the metal's job in a thermometer, where it climbs the tube as it warms.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicksilver is an old name for mercury, the liquid metal that expands up a thermometer tube when heat increases.

clue.text: Gentle but earthy heirs

explanation.surface: Mild-mannered people are the ones who will come into the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition echoes the Beatitude: 'Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.'
explanation.definitionFit: The meek are mild and humble; the Sermon on the Mount promises that the humble shall inherit the world.

clue.text: Freshman taking wife to South Pacific islands

parts.note: fresh means new and man gives the pronoun he, so the one word splits as fresh plus man
a bride is a newly married wife
S is the compass abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: A first-year student brings his wife on a trip to islands in the South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freshman' looks like a first-year student; split it as fresh (NEW) and man (HE).
explanation.definitionFit: The New Hebrides was the colonial name of the island group that became Vanuatu in the south-west Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Is it master's disposition to fail such an easy shot?

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters of the preceding words are set out again in a new order

parts.note: the S of master's counts as a letter in the fodder here

explanation.surface: A player wonders whether it is in a champion's nature to fluff a simple shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposition' reads as temperament, but it is the anagram signal for IS IT MASTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitter is an easy chance in sport, one any player should take; failing to score from it is a notorious blunder.

clue.text: I involved CID with fee as a put up job

indicators.note: involved means mixed up or entangled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written here as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A detective reports that the police CID and a payment were part of a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A put up job' suggests a frame-up, but here it is literal: something put up, a building.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large building, something erected or put up by builders.

clue.text: Every snare turned up corroded

parts.note: ea is the abbreviation for each, meaning every

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word for snare is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a net is a trap or snare

explanation.surface: Each trap was found rusted when overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal eaten away by rust or acid has been corroded.

clue.text: Furtively leave as petticoat seems to be showing

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks away when their underskirt starts to peep below the hem.
explanation.walkthrough: A slip is a petticoat; one hanging below a dress is said to be peeping out.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave without being noticed is to sneak away; an underskirt visible below a hem is protruding into view.

clue.text: Feed the ovens in the potteries

explanation.surface: A worker keeps the kilns burning in the china-making towns.
explanation.walkthrough: The Potteries are the six towns of north Staffordshire, England, famous for china; Stoke-on-Trent is their city.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a furnace going you add fuel to it; the city at the centre of England's china trade bears the same name.

clue.text: Poor Scottish banker very dry inside

indicators.note: inside says the letters for very dry go within the river's name

parts.note: a banker in crosswords is a river, something with banks; the Tay is Scotland's longest river
TT means teetotal, someone who never drinks, so very dry

explanation.surface: A poor Scottish bank manager is completely teetotal at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' looks like a financier but is the crossword river, a thing with banks; 'very dry' is the British TT for a teetotaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby or worn, of poor quality.

clue.text: Unnamed fellow circulating outsize stockings

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the pronoun goes round the size letters

parts.note: a man not named is simply he
OS is the abbreviation for outsize in clothing

explanation.surface: A man going round in oversized stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose is the old collective word for stockings and tights.

clue.text: A royal refusal given a Florentine runner

parts.note: R stands for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A king or queen says no to a runner from Florence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' means a river here, a thing that runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arno is the river that flows through Florence in Tuscany.

clue.text: Yanks in physical training?

explanation.surface: Americans doing their exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yanks' looks like Americans but is the verb, to pull sharply; physical jerks are old British slang for drill exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp tugs are pulls; physical jerks were the drill exercises done in gym classes.

clue.text: A trip for nothing but pleasure, perhaps

definitions.text: A trip for nothing but pleasure, perhaps

parts.words: A trip for nothing but pleasure, perhaps
parts.note: describes a drive taken purely for fun and at no cost to the driver, the car being someone else's taken without leave

explanation.surface: A holiday outing taken purely to enjoy oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For nothing' means both 'free' and 'with no other aim': the trip is a thrill ride in a stolen car.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless drive in a car taken without the owner's consent, purely for the thrill.

clue.text: Company submerged in great wave causes widespread affliction

indicators.note: submerged in means sunk inside, so the abbreviation goes inside the word for the wave

parts.note: a surge is a great rush or wave of water

explanation.surface: A firm swamped by a tidal wave brings misery to a wide area.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a cause of great suffering, such as a plague afflicting many.

clue.text: The fool's in favour, blow it!

indicators.note: in places the fool inside the word for favour

parts.note: a boon is a favour or blessing
an ass is a fool; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that a silly person has been given preference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow it!' reads as a mild curse, but it is an instruction: this is an instrument you blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassoon is a woodwind instrument, played by blowing into its double reed.

clue.text: The mortal moon hath her endur'd (Shakespeare Sonnet 107)

definitions.text: The mortal moon hath her endur'd (Shakespeare Sonnet 107)

parts.words: The mortal moon hath her endur'd (Shakespeare Sonnet 107)
parts.note: a quotation with a word missing between her and endur'd; the gap is filled with the darkening the moon suffers

explanation.surface: A line of Shakespeare's verse about the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: Sonnet 107 reads 'The mortal moon hath her eclipse endur'd': the missing word is the one to supply.
explanation.definitionFit: When the earth's shadow falls on the moon it is obscured, the event the sonnet's line describes.

clue.text: Jot a letter to Mr Karamanlis?

explanation.surface: Write a quick note to a Greek statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jot' looks like a verb but is the noun, a tiny amount; Konstantinos Karamanlis was a Greek prime minister, so his letters are Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount is a jot, from the smallest Greek character; that character is one a Greek politician would write.

clue.text: 5's opposite number among the stock dealers

definitions.text: 5's opposite number among the stock dealers

parts.words: 5's opposite number among the stock dealers
parts.note: on the stock exchange the optimist who expects prices to rise is matched by a pessimist who sells expecting them to fall

explanation.surface: The counterpart of another trader on the exchange floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue points back to 5-down: on the stock market the two animals stand for rising and falling prices.
explanation.definitionFit: A speculator who sells shares expecting their price to fall, the counterpart of the optimistic buyer.

clue.text: Slight legato effect

explanation.surface: A small musical smoothness in the playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective but is the noun or verb, an insult; in music notation a curved line joins notes to be played smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: An insult is a slur; a curved mark joining notes so they are played legato is also given that name.

clue.text: A load to carry round before sun-up

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word sun is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone carries a heavy load around before the sun rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun-up' looks like dawn; split it as the word sun with 'up', which in a down clue reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility one must bear.

clue.text: Make a judgment using pencil and measuring rod?

explanation.surface: A judge decides the case with a pencil and ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruling is an official decision, and ruling is also drawing straight lines with a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge or referee pronounces a decision; drawing lines with a ruler is ruling a page.

clue.text: The first lady right, continually

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible's Genesis story

explanation.surface: The president's wife is always correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife, but it is Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means always or at all times, a synonym of continually.

clue.text: A flier automatically getting angry though the award couldn't be higher

parts.note: George was RAF slang for an aircraft's automatic pilot
cross means angry

explanation.surface: An autopilot gets cross even though it has received the highest honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' was wartime RAF slang for the autopilot. The George Cross is the highest British award for civilian gallantry.
explanation.definitionFit: The George Cross is Britain's top decoration for bravery not in the face of the enemy, ranking with the Victoria Cross.
